edit.description: `shellGate` and the three package-manager gates built from it
the declared command gate, held to one span because its child reads per-span facts
the builtins' declaration and a batch handed to one
the width a phase gated by builtins reaches
the declared command gate still holding its phase to one span

summary: the shell-backed builtins declare `batches: true`, so a chain raising `mergeBatch` over them reaches a batched merge instead of silently staying serial
acceptance: a phase whose `afterMerge` gates are shell-backed builtins merges at the width the chain declared, a declared command gate still holds its phase to one span per merge, and a batch handed to a builtin runs one command over the merged tree
tests: shellGate declares that it reads a batch
tsc, vitest and eslint gates declare that they read a batch
a phase whose afterMerge gates are shell-backed builtins merges at the declared width
a declared command gate holds its phase to one span per merge
notes: The section's reason for withholding a batch is that a gate written for one entry would read a batch's facts as one entry's; a shell-backed gate reads none — verdict is exit code alone, and its only context read is `cwd` (`spec/chain.md`, *The builtin gates*). The declared command gate is the opposite: `gateFacts` builds `FLUME_BASE_SHA` and friends off a single-span context, and the env has no batch spelling.
